subject: Quantify Labs — dedicated capacity matrix and traffic details
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@quantifylabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: solutions@quantifylabs.com
Date: 2028-03-15 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing intake — initial traffic snapshot attached

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking the time to chat yesterday. As discussed, we're evaluating a dedicated fleet with Redwood for our real-time summarization and assistant endpoints. I've attached a small traffic snapshot (CSV) and a short list of canonical prompts so you can get started on a sizing estimate. High-level:

- Peak inbound requests: 38 RPS (observed 95th = 33 RPS)
- Concurrent sessions: average 28, typical peak 42
- Prompt size (tokens): median 120, 95th 750
- Average response expected: ~300 tokens
- Burst patterns: short spikes up to ~65 RPS for 30–90s during product events
- Preferred model family: want to test both an Llama-derived 13B quantized option and a 70B fp16 family; flexibility for fallbacks is fine

We also have strict PII retention rules and need audit logs; happy to answer more detailed security questions in parallel. Can you confirm what additional fields you need in the template?

Attachments: quantify_traffic_snapshot.csv, sample_prompts.txt

Thanks,
Ava
Head of Platform — Quantify Labs
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@quantifylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial traffic snapshot attached

Hi Ava — great context, thanks for the snapshot. I uploaded a concise template (attached) that helps us map traffic to GPU SKUs and autoscale policy. A few clarifying items so we size conservatively:

1) Traffic shape and peaks
- Are the 30–90s spikes predictable around scheduled events, or truly ad hoc? Predictable spikes can be handled with short burst capacity; ad hoc requires higher baseline or faster spin-up.

2) Concurrency semantics
- You noted "concurrent sessions" — does that equal concurrent in-flight token generation, or concurrent open user sessions with long-lived context but infrequent token generation?

3) Response latency SLO
- What percent of requests need sub-300ms p50/p95 for the primary assistant path? For example, do you need 95% ≤ 500ms? This drives single-request batching and preferred GPU class.

4) Cost vs latency tradeoffs
- Are you okay with a quantized 13B baseline for most requests and an on-fallback to 70B for high-quality outputs? Or do you require the 70B to be primary for all traffic?

5) Persistence and KV cache rules
- Typical session lengths and whether you expect reuse of KV cache across requests (helpful to determine cache hit rates).

If you can populate the attached dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx with per-endpoint RPS, p50/p95 prompt/response token estimates, and daily burst windows, we can turn this into a preliminary fleet matrix (GPU SKUs, pool sizes, expected token cost) within 48 hours. I cc'd Marissa for mapping to GPU SKUs and Dev for any runtime constraints (quantization/batching guidance).

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

Best,
Mateo
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial traffic snapshot attached

Looping in some internal sizing notes for the matrix. Mateo — quick internal checklist before we finalize the matrix:

- If Quantify is ok with 13B quantized as primary, we can map ~1.8–2.2k generated tokens/sec per A10G-equivalent node under our batching profile (assuming 95ms tail latencies at p95 for single-turn). For 70B fp16 primary, we typically plan 6–8 concurrent requests per A100s-equivalent with a higher token cost.
- Need the p95 latency SLO to decide on whether to prioritize low-batch, low-latency kernels vs high-throughput kernels.
- Burst capacity: propose a short-burst pool sized at +1.5x observed peak for 2-minute windows to avoid queuing.
- Autoscale spin-up: confirm whether Quantify requires "instant" burst (<30s). If yes, we should add reserved warm nodes.

Dev — can you confirm our current recommended quantized 13B artifact (INT8/FP16 hybrid) supports prefix KV reuse across session windows and the expected KV cache memory per session if they keep 4–6k tokens? I'll sketch a sample fleet matrix once we have the filled template — include per-endpoint buckets (assistant, summarization, reranker) so we can split pools if they want per-SLA isolation.

Marissa
Pre-Sales Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava@quantifylabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: solutions@quantifylabs.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-17 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing intake — initial traffic snapshot attached

Thanks — filled the template and attached more detailed per-endpoint numbers. Quick answers inline and in the sheet:

- Spikes: 80% of spikes are scheduled (marketing/demos), but 20% are ad hoc. We want to avoid degraded UX during ad hoc bursts.
- Concurrency: concurrent sessions == in-flight token generation; most sessions generate tokens continuously for 10–30s.
- Latency SLO: target p50 ≤ 200ms, p95 ≤ 600ms for the assistant endpoint; summarization can tolerate p95 ≤ 1.2s.
- Model preference: want 13B quantized as baseline with a small reserve of 70B for high-fidelity answers.
- KV cache: sessions typically keep ~3–5k tokens; reuse is high within a session.

Attachments: quantify_traffic_snapshot.csv (revised), sample_prompts.txt, filled_dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

Next steps: once you produce the preliminary fleet matrix, can we schedule a 45m sizing walkthrough next week (preferably Tue/Wed PST)? Also please include estimated monthly token spend and suggested warm-node buffer for ad hoc bursts.

Appreciate it —
Ava
Head of Platform — Quantify Labs
